Verified reference: Šimić, Veas and Sabol, “A comprehensive analysis of perturbation methods in explainable AI feature attribution validation for neural time series classifiers,” Scientific Reports 15, 26607, published 22 July 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41598-025-09538-2. Experiments cover five datasets, five neural architectures, 12 attribution methods, 23 perturbation methods and two region sizes. The proposed Consistency-Magnitude-Index combines consistency and magnitude of differences between most-relevant-first and least-relevant-first perturbation curves. [Original paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-09538-2)

Main findings: perturbation choice can change explanation rankings; no method works best across datasets, architectures and classes. Smaller regions generally yield higher faithfulness scores, although interpolation methods benefit from larger regions. Zero, sample-mean and Laplace perturbations perform well as defaults; evaluation should nevertheless use diverse perturbations. A confidence collapse after modifying supposedly irrelevant features can indicate perturbation-induced distribution shift, making confidence drops alone misleading evidence of importance. [Methods and findings](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-09538-2)

Implication for the recommendation diagnostic: methodological support for comparing relevant versus irrelevant history perturbations and checking sensitivity to perturbation type and region size. This is an extrapolation: the study evaluates time-series classification confidence, not categorical recommendation histories, ranking quality, HR@10, or latent user traits. It therefore motivates diagnostic controls but does not directly validate the proposed recommendation diagnostic.
